name: Inside the room
status: approved by the owner on 2026-11-07: these criteria, the time-box and the AI budget (spec 2.2, touchpoint 2), as drafted in docs/rungs/2/plan.md, with the agent-seeing additions A1, A2 (three rules), A3 and A4 (O6) and every other decision as the plan recommends (O2-O13)

ai_budget.plan: the owner's current Claude plan, nothing else (P1 default)
ai_budget.note: Usage is logged per session in PROGRESS.md; a task with its reviewer subagent counts as one session. The 52 are the base rung's 43 (the 12 sessions logged before approval, then T5-T25, 22 units with T23 the two rung reviews, at 1b's 1.37 sessions per planned unit) and 9 for A1-A4 (6 units). The pivot rule (spec 7.7) compares rungs 1a-3 against twice their time-boxes.

features.description: `play --map room --windowed --ticks 600 --seed 1 --input room-walk.input.toml --hashes h.txt` presents first-person frames in a real window (under xvfb on Linux), and h.txt equals the committed hashes/room-walk.seed1.txt.

Hash streams are identical on the five native targets, the PR-tier Linux targets and RISC-V, and equal the committed streams. The five dot streams are unchanged from rung 1b (O12 leaves pmove as it is); the room streams, sim-data hash included, are identical on every target.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test | riscv | native | summary

features.description: eng-collision-grid passes the collision conformance suite with ADR-0024's contact rule (exact on axis faces, within CONTACT_GAP off the axes), and gives the brute-force oracle's Trace bits on proptest maps and sweeps.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test (step collision) | riscv

features.description: kit-fps's ground movement: steps up to 0.4 m climb and 0.41 m blocks, the hull snaps down to the ground, gravity acts only in the air, slopes steeper than the floor limit are not climbed, and the hull is never inside solid; with a flat-ground proptest over the grid.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test (step movement) | riscv

features.description: The room's snapshot fits 1,200 bytes. Sim data is outside the state, its hash and snapshots; sim_data_hash is in recordings, reports and the room's hash-stream header, and changes with the room's data only; the dot map's is 0.

The render graph's oracles: any declaration order gives one graph or one error; culling, bypass, continues and pooling as ADR-0019 says; GPU labels set. Graph::new, Graph::fixed and rung 1b's counters are unchanged.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test (step render-graph) | native (step tests)

features.description: The structured look checks, exact on every adapter: every look switch off gives the plain pipeline's image; with the palette on, every pixel is a palette colour; on a flat material, banding gives at most 32 levels per region; fog moves monotonically toward its colour with depth along a probe row; the tone curve is within one 8-bit level of a CPU reference on a ramp. Each look pass switches off alone.

Sprite rotations match an independent f64 atan2 oracle, the hand-checked cases, the tie rule and the mirror flags; billboards turn about Z only; the alpha test writes depth, so a thing behind the pillar is hidden.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test (step sprites) | native (step look)

features.description: Mouse look follows the plan's decision 9 (integer sensitivity, signs, exact rounding, the pitch limit), checked against an independent oracle; the same motion timeline gives the same PlayerCommands on every target (proptest).

The headless platform records cursor and fullscreen requests (the new conformance suite); `play --report` names the cursor grab mode, fullscreen and the refresh rate; losing focus releases the cursor.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job native (steps window-room, tests)

features.description: On macos-26 the GCMouse shim (eng-platform-gcmouse, the only crate with unsafe code, ADR-0021) builds and its tests with a fake source pass. The runner has no mouse, so nothing here reads a real GCMouse.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job native (step tests on macos-26)

features.description: On ubuntu-24.04 (x64), every shot in shots.toml, rung 1b's four and rung 2's first-person ones, equals its golden exactly. The adapter is Mesa 25.2.7 lavapipe with a fixed llvmpipe environment.
On the other four native runners, every shot's FLIP error against the same goldens is within its limits in golden/thresholds.toml.

The shot harness on the owner's M2 Pro is within the limits, and shots.json records the macOS and Metal driver versions. An agent runs it on the Mac and the owner confirms. CI does not compute this feature.
Instruction counts for both simulation steps, grid traces and ground_move on ubuntu-24.04 x64. More than 5% over the push's base fails unless the push adds a performance ADR naming the benchmark.

docs-check also checks that every cargo xtask command, probe command, path, ENG_* variable and [E-*] tag named in AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md exists; a stale path fails.
features.command: cargo xtask docs-check && cargo xtask selftest docs-stale-path

features.description: The notices list every third-party crate in the testbed binary for the three playable targets, with licence texts; a licence off deny.toml's list fails.

`cargo xtask dist` makes an archive holding the stripped binary, its debug info, version.json and the notices; the unpacked binary runs `--version --json` and `run --headless --ticks 60`. No tags, release or signing.

Over the rung's core changes (the diff from 314383d, the commit that added docs/rungs/2/plan.md, Q2's ground_move included), no missed mutant outside .cargo/mutants.toml's exclusions. Pending on push runs; the weekly schedule and a manual dispatch run it.
Each of these fails, with a self-test: unsafe code outside the GCMouse shim's one module; objc2-game-controller used outside the shim; a stale path in the docs; a missed mutant.
features.command: cargo xtask selftest unsafe-outside-shim && cargo xtask selftest gcmouse-outside-shim && cargo xtask selftest docs-stale-path && cargo xtask selftest mutant-missed

features.description: As rung 1b's: reports record the adapter and its capabilities, and per-frame counts are within budgets.toml [gpu]. Also a first-person room shot within a new [gpu.first_person] table, and per-pass GPU times (or null) and the pool's texture count in new gpu keys. per_frame, tier 0 and the capability names stay as shot_video.rs pins them.
CI writes proof.apng, the scripted dot-square session, and room.apng, the 600-tick room walk, as artifacts; the owner also gets them as local files.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job native (step proof-video on ubuntu-24.04)

features.description: On the owner's Mac: fullscreen, mouse look, WASD, the step, turning sprites, the --look switches, and Esc quits. The owner plays it and accepts it. CI does not compute this feature.

On the owner's Mac, while the mouse moves fast, the GCMouse shim's callbacks per second exceed the display's refresh rate (`play --report`). An agent runs it there and the owner confirms. CI does not compute this feature.
features.command: cargo run -p game-testbed -- play --map room --report r.json

features.description: Agent seeing A1: `shot` and `video` write <out>.frame.json (the camera; each object's id, kind and world box; from the info and output targets, each object's visible pixels, screen box, mean luminance and contrast against its surroundings; depth at a fixed 8x6 grid of probes; a luminance histogram). There is a record for every shot, exact on the pinned lavapipe and within per-shot tolerances elsewhere; a planted not-drawn bug and a drawn-black bug each change it.

Agent seeing A2: protected <scene>.rules.toml files, checked by a script over frame records, with three rules: an object marked must_see has at least 50 visible pixels and contrast at least 0.1; no first-person pixel shows the clear colour; floor shows in the lower third and ceiling or sky in the upper third. Every shot passes, and each rule has a self-test that breaks it.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job native (step scene-rules) && cargo xtask selftest rule-1 (and rule-2, rule-3)

features.description: Agent seeing A3: `shot --pose x,y,z,yaw,pitch` gives a camera independent of movement; shots.toml names poses. Every named pose renders on every runner, and the report's views equal the manifest.

Agent seeing A4: 12 planted render bugs, written by an agent that did not build the renderer, as patches that `cargo xtask selftest render-bug-<n>` applies to a workspace copy. Every planted bug fails a check that is not hard-coded to one scene, or is a known miss the owner accepted; a deletion run and a bug-by-check table go in PROGRESS.md.

Carried from rung 1b: the workspace builds and every test passes on the five native runners (ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, windows-2025, windows-11-arm, macos-26), and `cargo check --target x86_64-apple-darwin` passes on macos-26.
Carried from rung 1b: `play --ticks 240 --seed 1 --input dot-square.input.toml --hashes h.txt` opens a real window (under xvfb on Linux), and h.txt equals the committed hashes/dot-square.seed1.txt.
Carried from rung 1b: a running `play` gets Escape from xdotool through the real OS path and exits 0 within 5 s; a headless-twin test covers every target.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job native (step esc on ubuntu-24.04, tests everywhere)

features.description: Carried from rung 1b: a panic in `run` and in `play` writes crash.json with every field (version stamp, thread, backtrace, last log lines, seed, tick, command line) and exits 12. The test job has no display, so it checks `run` only.
Carried from rung 1b: `--version --json` prints every field of version.json, and `--version` prints the same stamp on one line. A CI build has no `unknown`.
Carried from rung 1b: every WGSL file validates with naga and translates to SPIR-V, MSL and HLSL.

Carried from rung 1b, unchanged (rung 2 changes no wire format): the eng-net-wire golden vectors hold and its decoders never panic (proptest). The session gives the same hashes as stepping the simulation directly.
features.command: cargo xtask ci --job test (step wire-session) | riscv

features.description: Carried from rung 1b: AGENTS.md is at most 150 lines.
